one_month_reasoning: No NVDA earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 reports 2026-11-17 (Yahoo/Wall Street Horizon calendars; EPS consensus ~$2.47 on a $108B guide), after 2026-11-04. Inside the window: TSMC Q3 results (mid-October; a read on N3/CoWoS AI demand), hyperscaler Q3 reports with 2027 capex guidance (MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN, roughly Oct 27-30) and the FOMC on Oct 28, where prediction markets price ~17% odds of a hike (DeFi Rate aggregator of Kalshi/Polymarket, 2026-10-05) with the 10Y already at ~5.26%. Alt-data does not point to a demand break: the H100 rental index is flat over 4 weeks and +14% y/y (re-checked 2026-10-05). Hyperscaler capex guides lean slightly positive, but the stock sits at its 52-week high after a +24.9% year and a hawkish FOMC surprise is a modest downside risk, so I stay close to symmetric: a lognormal centred on $238 (+0.5% drift) with monthly sigma 11.5% (38%/3.5, a little wider for the capex-guide and FOMC event risk). Unchanged from round 1; the supervisor's findings concern the 12-month valuation, not the 1-month window.

fair_value.method: Blend, 12 months out: 60% P/E (consistent-basis NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of ~$17.5 x 17x = $297.5) and 40% FCF yield (NTM FCF ~$13.1/share at 75% conversion / 4.5% yield + ~$1 net cash = $293). Gives ~$296, down from $303. The 17x is 2.5 turns below today's ~19.5x NTM; break-even for a flat year is ~13.5x.

Within the peer range (6.1x-128.9x, median 35x), near the low large-cap cluster (AVGO 20.5x, TSM 20.7x, QCOM 20.0x). Two turns below NVDA's current 19.3x: the forward P/E fell from ~40 to ~19 over the year as EPS more than doubled (src 3, 4, 14). Capital Blueprint expects 15-18x if growth slows toward ~50%. The supervisor's evidence that compression has been estimate-driven (FY28 EPS up ~24% in 90 days while price rose) argues against assuming more than 2.5 turns; the verified 10Y at ~5.26% and ~75% December-hike odds (sources 23, 24) argue against assuming less. Break-even is ~13.5x on $17.5, so 17x already absorbs ~13% compression from 19.5x

bear.story: By mid-2027 an AI capex digestion is visible: hyperscalers guide CY2028 capex flat, ASIC share gains (TPU, Trainium, MTIA) show up in inference, memory costs hold GM near 70%, and receivables (DSO 60, five customers ~70% of AR) and the $279B supply commitments turn into a write-down or pull-in story; higher rates (10Y ~5.3%) make the de-rating sharper. NTM EPS about $13.75 at a MU-style peak-cycle 12x. This is the EPS-break case the supervisor identifies as the one that matters, not plain compression.

base.story: FY28 roughly delivers the ~70% supply-constrained guide (verified in the transcript) and GM settles at 72-73%, but by late 2027 the debate moves to FY29 growth of 20-25%. Compression continues to ~16x on ~$17 consistent-basis NTM EPS. Earnings growth beats multiple compression, so the stock grinds higher, as it did this year (+25% while EPS doubled).

bull.story: Checkable trigger: the formal FY28 outlook in late-Feb 2027 is at or above +75% (vs the ~70% preliminary), DSO falls back below 50 days by the Q1 FY28 print (May 2027), and the Q2 FY28 call (Aug 2027) points to FY29 growth of 30%+. Then the multiple holds ~20x (inside the AVGO/TSM ~20.6x cluster, no premium) on ~$20 NTM EPS. Trimmed from 21-22x / $425 / 23% because the supervisor flagged it as the panel's most generous and the SemiAnalysis upside claim is unverified at source.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 6.1x (MU) to 128.9x (ARM); fwd EV/EBITDA ~4.4x to ~125x. Forward EV/EBITDA is my proxy: trailing EV/EBITDA x (fwd P/E / ttm P/E). Growth is the implied ttm-to-forward EPS step-up, also my calculation from the same pages.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17x NTM P/E (consistent Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29 basis): inside the range, at about the 15th percentile, below the 35x median and just under the large-cap cluster of AVGO 20.5x, TSM 20.7x and QCOM 20.0x. NVDA trades at ~19.5x on the matching basis today (stockanalysis 19.34x). The bull case uses ~20x, inside that cluster. Note the EV/EBITDA forward values are my proxy, not vendor forward estimates.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: I apply a discount to the median, not a premium, and keep the multiple inside the peer range. The median is inflated by early-ramp names (ARM, AMD, MRVL) whose ttm earnings are depressed. The closest analogues for a mega-cap at peak-cycle margins are the low cluster and MU (6x), which shows how the market capitalises earnings it thinks are cyclical. Reasons NVDA sits in the low cluster: (1) growth is set to slow from ~70% to ~20-25% within the horizon; (2) earnings quality has softened, with OCF/NI at 0.40 in Q2, DSO from 45 to 60 days, $279B supply commitments and a $105B guarantee tied to OpenAI infrastructure; (3) GM is being reset down to 71-73% by memory costs; (4) at a $5.7T market cap and ~7.4% S&P weight, mandate limits cap incremental demand. No premium is argued.

thesis_break_reason: $165 is just below the 52-week low ($164.27), about 10x my FY28 EPS of ~$16 and ~9.4x consistent-basis Oct-2027 NTM EPS, about 30% below today and well under the ~13.5x break-even multiple. At that level the market would most likely be pricing a failure of the ~70% FY28 guide (a hyperscaler capex cut, losses to ASICs, or customer financing stress in the extended receivables and guarantees), not ordinary 38%-vol noise. Unchanged in round 2: the supervisor's corrections move value by ~2%, not the break level.

reasoning: Round 2 revision after the supervisor's fact-check. What changed: (1) FCF leg. The supervisor showed my 4.5% yield at 80% conversion valued the same earnings ~5% above my own P/E leg, and that Q2 conversion was 36-39% (CFO commentary: FCF $21.3B vs $59.7B GAAP NI; DSO 45 to 60; H1 FCF $69.9B). I cut conversion to 75%, kept a 4.5% yield (slightly stricter than the 4.41% that a 17x P/E implies at 75%) and added true net cash of $23.2B (~$1/share, excluding $42.8B of equity stakes per the 10-Q). FCF leg $311 to $293. (2) P/E leg unchanged: my NTM window (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) was confirmed consistent with today's 19.5x basis and $17.5 sits in the supervisor's consensus-based $17.4-17.8 range. I keep 17x rather than moving to the supervisor's 16.5x: compression has been estimate-driven, and I already take 2.5 turns off; the verified 5.26% 10Y stops me from assuming less. Fair value $303 to $296. (3) SemiAnalysis: I found the claim recapped by Yahoo (2026-06-30), but that is a press recap of the same X post, it predates the Q3 guide of $108B, and the SemiAnalysis newsletter itself (March) says only that supply, not demand, binds. It stays out of the numbers and out of the bull story. (4) Bull case tied to a checkable trigger (FY28 formal guide >=75%, DSO <50, FY29 30%+) and trimmed to $400 at 20%. Bear at $165/28%, base $272/52%. Scenario mean ~$268, median ~$263, below the $296 fair value because fair value assumes the base EPS path is delivered while the distribution carries a 28% EPS-break tail. Key frame from the supervisor that I accept: the stock is flat at ~13.5x consistent NTM EPS, so losing money needs an EPS break, not just compression; my bear tail is sized for that. Alt-data re-checked: H100 rental index flat over 4 weeks, +14% y/y, so no glut signal. Ladder is a mixture of lognormals (sigma 0.25/0.19/0.20) with a slightly fatter far-right tail; P(>=237) falls 0.647 to 0.618 and upper strikes fall 2-4pp. 1-month ladder unchanged. Option-implied data and priors/ were not consulted; X was read only via snippets.
